fields.meta_title: JHA Form Template Crews Sign on Their Phones | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a JHA form template your crew fills in on a phone, with job steps, hazards, controls ranked by type, and signatures in a database you own.
fields.h1: Build a JHA Form Template Crews Sign Before Work
fields.hero_description: Build a JHA form template that lists each job step with its hazards and controls and gets crew signatures before work starts.
fields.features_heading: What the Crew Checks Before the Job Starts
fields.features_subheading: A paper JHA gets read once and filed. Build the form with Emergent, and the next crew opens the same steps and signatures.
fields.feature_1:
Steps listed in the order the job runs

Each job step gets its own row, in the order the worker does it. Under every step, the form lists what can go wrong, how badly someone could be hurt, and the controls set for it.
fields.feature_2:
Controls tagged engineering, admin, or PPE

Every control carries a type: engineering, administrative, or PPE. A hazard whose only control is PPE gets a flag and goes to the safety manager before the crew starts work.
fields.feature_3:
Crew signatures on one phone

Each worker reads the steps and signs on the crew lead's phone or on their own. The app records who signed and at what time, and a job still missing a signature shows as not ready.
fields.feature_4:
A new version asks for new signatures

Change a step or a control, and the app saves the JHA as a new version and asks every worker on that job to sign it again. The old version and its signatures stay on file beside it.
fields.feature_5:
A review when an injury names the job

An injury or near-miss report that names a job marks that job's JHA for review and emails the safety lead. The JHA stays marked until someone signs off on the revised version.
fields.feature_6:
Every JHA in a database you own

Keep every JHA, signature, and revision in a database you own. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and run the form next to the rest of your safety program.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Crews and the JHA Each One Signs
fields.tab_content_1:
No tear-off until each of the 4 crew signs

Jorund Pell leads a crew of 4 at Thornbeck Roofing, and every reroof begins with tear-off. On the driveway, he opens the tear-off JHA on his phone and reads its 5 steps aloud, starting with setting the roof anchors. Each crew member signs on the same phone. The job shows Ready only once all 4 signatures are in.
fields.tab_content_2:
Its only control was boots, and it went to Isaura

Grinding castings at Brisbourne Castings starts with lifting a 15-pound casting. Step 1 of the JHA lists a dropped casting, and its only control was steel-toe boots, tagged PPE. The app flagged it as PPE only and sent it to safety manager Isaura Velloway. She added an engineering control: a table beside the grinder.
fields.tab_content_3:
Each injury on the restack job reopens its JHA

A worker at Gorsedge Freight strained his back restacking pallets, and the injury report names step 3, lifting cartons from the floor. The app moved the pallet restack JHA to Under review and emailed safety lead Stellan Quaye. Until he signs a revised version, every crew that opens the JHA sees it marked Under review.
fields.tab_content_4:
3 of 12 still unsigned, each getting a morning email

Larkmoor Facilities rewrote its boiler room JHA to add a lockout step before any burner work. All 12 technicians on the job have to sign the new version, and 9 of 12 have signed. Each of the 3 still unsigned gets an email every morning, and maintenance manager Radomir Thornbeck sees their names on the dashboard.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a JHA Form Template
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to set up a JHA form template your crews sign before work, with hazards and ranked controls for each job step.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Watch the job before you write a step
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask the crew what goes wrong
fields.howto_step_1_des: List the jobs where an injury could be severe or disabling, even if nobody has been hurt doing them yet. OSHA gives priority to jobs like these, even with no history of accidents. Write one JHA per job, and start with the worst three.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Stand beside a worker while they do the job and write down each step as they take it, which is how OSHA's guide says to begin. Keep every step to one short action, such as lifting the casting. Aim for 5 to 8 steps per job.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Read the steps back to the people who do the job and ask what can go wrong at each one. OSHA notes that involving employees helps minimize oversights. Add a severity field, and sort the hazards by it.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Add a type field to each control with three choices: engineering, administrative, and PPE. OSHA ranks engineering controls as the most effective of the three. Flag a hazard that lists PPE as its only control, and send it to the safety manager.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Describe the jobs, the step and hazard fields, the control types, who signs, and who hears about a PPE-only flag in one prompt. Emergent builds the form and its database. Ask for later changes the same way, such as adding a job.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Connect your injury report to the job it names, and have that report put the job's JHA under review. OSHA calls a review particularly important after an illness or injury on a specific job. When the JHA changes, ask every worker on it to sign again.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill in one JHA yourself with a hazard that has only PPE listed, and sign it from two phones. Check that the flag reaches the safety manager and that the job shows Ready only after both signatures. Then delete the test entry and share the form.

faq_plan.q: What is a JHA form template?
faq_plan.a: A JHA form template is a reusable form for a job hazard analysis, which OSHA describes as a technique that focuses on job tasks as a way to identify hazards before they occur. Each copy covers one job: its steps in order, the hazards at each step, and the controls for each hazard.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a JHA form template?
faq_plan.a: Describe your jobs and who signs to Emergent's AI form builder, and it builds the JHA form along with its database. Then fill in one test JHA with a crew member and fix anything that reads wrong before you share the link.

faq_plan.q: Which jobs should a JHA form template cover first?
faq_plan.a: Start with the jobs where a mistake could cause a severe or disabling injury. OSHA gives priority to jobs with the potential to cause those injuries, even if there is no history of previous accidents. After that, work through jobs with the most recorded injuries and any job you changed recently.

faq_plan.q: Who fills in the JHA form template for a job?
faq_plan.a: A supervisor or safety lead fills it out together with the workers who do the job. OSHA says involving employees will help minimize oversights and ensure a quality analysis, and its guide suggests watching an employee perform the job while listing each step. Tell the worker you are judging the job, not them.

faq_plan.q: What order should controls go in on a JHA form template?
faq_plan.a: Put engineering controls first, then administrative controls, then PPE. OSHA calls engineering controls that physically change a machine or work environment the most effective, with administrative controls next when those are not feasible. It accepts PPE when engineering controls are not feasible or do not totally eliminate the hazard.

faq_plan.q: How often should a completed JHA form template be reviewed?
faq_plan.a: Review it on a schedule you set, such as once a year, and right after any illness or injury on that job, a review OSHA calls particularly important. Review it again whenever the steps or tools change. Any time you revise a JHA, OSHA says to train all employees affected by the changes. Collect a fresh signature from each of them.

faq_plan.q: What fields does a simple JHA form template need?
faq_plan.a: A simple JHA form template needs the job title, location, the person doing the analysis, and the date. Then add a repeating section for each step with the hazard, how severe it could be, and the controls with their type. End with a signature line for every worker on the job. Emergent builds those fields from a plain-English prompt, and you change them the same way.

faq_plan.q: Can workers sign a JHA form template on their phones?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the form is built to capture signatures. An app built with Emergent can capture an e-signature from each worker on a phone, record when each one signed, and hold the job at Not ready until every name on the crew list has signed.

faq_plan.q: Where should a JHA form template store completed JHAs?
faq_plan.a: Store completed JHAs where a supervisor can pull up the current version for any job in seconds, with every past version and its signatures kept beside it. Keep them for as long as your own records policy says. A JHA app built with Emergent keeps them in a database you own, with no response caps on how many crews submit.

faq_plan.q: What should a hazard description say on a JHA form template?
faq_plan.a: Say what could go wrong at that step, who or what it would happen to, what sets it off, and the result. For example: while lifting a casting from the bin, the worker could drop it on a foot and break toes. A vague entry such as "lifting hazard" gives the next crew nothing to control.

plan.angle: The top 10 for jha form template is downloadable PDF, Word and Excel sheets plus OSHA's own booklet: a grid for job steps, hazards and controls that someone fills in once and files. scope.evidence: H1 "Build a JHA Form Template Crews Sign Before Work", title and hero (125 chars) cover the whole job: steps, hazards, controls, crew signatures; how-to description one sentence, 121 chars.

intent.evidence: Top 10 is printable JHA sheets plus OSHA 3071; page gives the same grid (feature 1, FAQ 7 field list, FAQ 10 hazard wording) and the OSHA method (how-to 1-4, FAQ 3-6) as a phone app.

specificity.evidence: Buyer vocabulary throughout: "engineering, administrative, or PPE", "PPE only", "tear-off", "lockout step before any burner work"; no hub boilerplate.

openers.evidence: Every paragraph opens on a full sentence: "Each job step gets its own row", "Grinding castings at Brisbourne Castings starts with lifting a 15-pound casting."

craft.evidence: No tacked-on endings; longest sentences 33 and 36 words (FAQ 1, 8) are under the 40 limit. Minor items recorded as notes.

voice.evidence: Plain verbs and concrete details: "a table beside the grinder", "9 of 12 have signed", "Each of the 3 still unsigned gets an email every morning".

truth.evidence: All 8 OSHA statements match their OSHA 3071 quotes in domain_sources (definition, priority jobs, watch the job, involve employees, engineering most effective, PPE when not feasible, review after injury, train after revision). Emergent claims map to prompt-build, e-signature-capture, alerts, database-owned, code-export, no-caps, free-start. Numbers agree across fields: 4 crew/4 signatures/5 steps, 15-pound casting step 1, step 3 lifting cartons, 9 of 12 and 3 unsigned. No safety guarantees anywhere.

distinct.evidence: Own page: PPE-only flag, injury-triggered review and re-sign on new version are JHA-specific; no sibling primaries in headings.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions, each answered in the first sentence; one hub link in item 2 ("AI form builder"), no forced sibling links; no brands or file formats in questions; Emergent lines in items 7, 8, 9 are claims-backed.

images.evidence: Contact sheet matches copy word for word: "4 of 4 signed"/"5 steps"/"Set roof anchors"; "Dropped 15-pound casting", "Steel-toe boots" PPE only, email to Isaura Velloway, "Table beside grinder"; "Step 3: lifting cartons from the floor" email to Stellan Quaye; "9 of 12 signed", "3 still unsigned", "On Radomir's dashboard". Alt text agrees; JHA cased correctly in every image.
